title: crosscheck-agent tool surface
description: Single source of truth for the tools exposed over MCP (JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio). Inputs are enforced at the server boundary; outputs are documented here and will be validated in P1.

ProviderArrayArg.description: Ad-hoc subset of provider names (e.g. ['openai','gemini','xai']). Omit to use the configured active set. Call list_providers first if you're unsure which names are available.

ProviderAnswer.description: One provider's response (or its failure mode) for a single turn.

response.description: The provider's text response. Mutually exclusive with `error`.

error_kind.description: Classified failure mode; drives retry policy and reporting.

retry_after_s.description: When the upstream sent a Retry-After header.

cache_hit.description: True if the response was served from the exact-match disk cache.

elapsed_ms.description: Wall-clock time the provider took (0 on cache hit).

attempts.description: Number of HTTP attempts made (1 = first try succeeded).

BudgetSummary.description: Per-call budget remaining at the moment the response was assembled.

RoleTurn.description: Role envelope produced by a single proposer/critic turn in coordinate.

ballot.description: Critic's stance on the proposal. Proposer always emits 'agree'.

StructuredSynthesis.description: Schema-validated synthesis output produced by the moderator/synthesizer role.

SessionSummary.description: Cumulative state for a session_id across calls.

PickScores.description: Per-provider scoring envelope for the pick tool: scores for every option across every criterion, plus an overall score per option in [0,1].

SolveVerifier.description: How to decide whether a proposal solves the problem. Either run a sandboxed subprocess (kind=shell) or pattern-match the proposal text (kind=regex_response).

cmd.description: argv for kind=shell. The proposal is fed to stdin.

memory_mb.description: Soft RLIMIT_AS cap on Unix; ignored on platforms without resource module.

Verifier.description: A rule-based check that runs against a provider's response text.

Golden.description: A bench fixture: an input + the rule-based assertions a passing answer must satisfy.

args.description: Args forwarded to the inner tool. The `providers` field is overridden per provider under bench.

ProviderErrorEnvelope.description: Returned when the caller asked for providers that aren't available; helps Claude self-correct.

list_providers.description: List every provider the server knows about and whether each is currently usable (has an API key in .env). Call this first to discover who's on the panel.

confer.description: Ask one or more LLMs the same question and return their answers in parallel.

auto_panel.description: When true (and `providers` not given), ask the smart router (`recommend_panel`) to pick the smallest effective panel for purpose='confer' from usage_log history. Ignored when `providers` is provided.

extract_claims.description: When true, an extra cheap-tier extractor call distills atomic claims with per-provider support/dissent maps. Adds one call's worth of cost; off by default.

early_stop.description: When true (and panel size >= 3), dispatch the first 2 panelists, ask a cheap-tier judge whether they agree on the headline, and skip the remaining panelists if confidence >= `early_stop_threshold`. Right-sized for low-stakes questions.

early_stop_threshold.description: Minimum agreement confidence required to short-circuit when `early_stop:true`.

session_id.description: Optional id to accumulate usage across calls.

untrusted_input.description: When true, treat `context` and `question` as untrusted: wrap in tags, neutralize obvious injection phrases, instruct panelists to treat as data only.

debate.description: Run a bounded multi-round debate across LLMs; moderator synthesises the result.

providers.description: Ad-hoc subset of provider names (e.g. ['openai','gemini','xai']). Omit to use the configured active set. Call list_providers first if you're unsure which names are available. Needs at least 2.

moderator.description: Provider name to run the synthesis round. Defaults to config.moderator.

auto_panel.description: When true (and `providers` not given), ask the smart router for the best debate panel from usage_log history.

auto_panel_n.description: Panel size when `auto_panel:true` (default 3 for debate; debate needs >= 2).

extract_claims.description: When true, an extra cheap-tier extractor call distills atomic claims from the FINAL round with per-provider support/dissent maps.

session_id.description: Optional id to accumulate usage across calls.

structured.description: If true, the moderator must emit a JSON object matching StructuredSynthesis. Validated server-side; one retry on failure with the validation errors fed back.

synthesis_errors.description: Validation errors when structured=true and the synthesizer's output didn't match the schema after retry.

plan.description: Collaborative planning across LLMs with risks + alternatives.

providers.description: Ad-hoc subset of provider names (e.g. ['openai','gemini','xai']). Omit to use the configured active set. Call list_providers first if you're unsure which names are available. Needs at least 2.

session_id.description: Optional id to accumulate usage across calls.

structured.description: If true, the moderator emits a JSON object matching StructuredSynthesis (validated server-side).

coordinate.description: Run a structured Proposer -> Critic(s) -> Synthesizer flow. The synthesizer's output is JSON-schema-validated; key claims, dissent, and open questions are persisted to the session claim-list when session_id is provided.

topic.description: What to coordinate on (question, decision, design).

proposer.description: Provider that drafts the initial proposal. Defaults to the first resolvable provider.

critics.description: Providers that critique the proposal in parallel. Defaults to all selected providers minus proposer/synthesizer.

synthesizer.description: Provider that produces the final structured synthesis. Defaults to the configured moderator.

session_id.description: Optional id; structured claims are persisted under this session.

delegate.description: Cross-model tool delegation with an explicit handshake. Run a delegable tool (confer or review) against a single named provider, with quota tracking by session_id and by requesting provider. Useful for capability handoffs ("route this code review to provider X") and for bounded multi-step plans where one model decides who answers a sub-question.

via.description: Provider that will execute the delegated call. Must be configured + within the provider_allowlist.

args.description: Arguments forwarded to the target tool. Any `providers` field is overridden to [via].

requested_by.description: Optional: provider on whose behalf this delegation is being made; counted toward its requester quota.

session_id.description: Optional id; counts toward the per-session delegation quota.

result.description: Forwarded output of the delegated tool when accepted.

triangulate.description: Run a Proposer/Critic/Synthesizer flow and return a consensus + minority report with per-provider weights drawn from accumulated ballot stats. Use this when you want one answer plus an honest dissenting view.

solve.description: Iteratively propose -> verify -> retry. The provider drafts a solution; the verifier (sandboxed shell command or regex on the proposal text) accepts or rejects it; on rejection the verifier output is fed back to the provider for one more pass, up to max_attempts. Returns the winning proposal (when solved) plus every attempt's record. NOTE: the 'sandbox' is a process timeout + soft memory cap — it is not network-isolation. Treat verifier commands as untrusted code execution and only run trusted scripts.

problem.description: The task to solve. The provider's response IS the proposal.

providers.description: Panel to draw from. Attempts rotate through providers; once exhausted the loop wraps.

target_path.description: Optional. When the proposal is a complete replacement file, set this to the absolute or repo-relative path of the file the proposal would replace. On a solved attempt, the result includes a `patch` field with a unified diff (current vs. proposal). The file is NOT modified — preview only.

patch.description: Unified diff (current target_path vs final_proposal). Present only when solved=true and target_path was given.

pick.description: Multi-criteria decision-making across a panel. Each provider scores every option on every criterion (0..1) plus an overall score, and the tool aggregates with criterion weights, returns a ranked list, surfaces the largest cross-provider disagreements as dissent_deltas, and writes the top-ranked option as a consensus claim when session_id is provided.

orchestrate.description: Plan-then-execute: the moderator decomposes the goal into a DAG of subtasks (or you pass a pre-authored `dag`), workers run in parallel where deps allow, and a final synthesizer recombines node outputs into a coherent deliverable. Each node declares `difficulty` (low|med|high) which feeds the cheap-mode router; with `cheap_mode:true` the cheapest sufficient model in the declared tier is picked per node. Default failure semantics: partial-recombine with [MISSING: ...] markers; set `fail_fast:true` for strict workflows. Every node's CPU/wall time and token cost is rolled up in the response `usage` + `timing` blocks.

goal.description: High-level goal; the moderator drafts the DAG. Mutually exclusive with `dag`.

dag.description: Pre-authored DAG; skips the planning round. Mutually exclusive with `goal`.

provider.description: Pin a specific provider for this node (overrides cheap-mode pick).

model.description: Pin a specific model for this node.

moderator.description: Provider used to plan the DAG and recombine the final result.

fail_fast.description: Stop on first node failure instead of partial-recombine with [MISSING: ...] markers.

cheap_mode.description: Route each node to the cheapest model in its declared difficulty tier.

plan_only.description: Return the resolved DAG with per-node provider/model + a coarse cost estimate WITHOUT running workers or recombine. The planner still runs (so a `goal` produces a DAG to display); only execution is skipped.

audit.description: Post-run audit: score an output (from `output_to_audit`, or pulled from the latest transcript for `session_id`) against a rubric. The auditor is selected to exclude the producing panel (`producing_panelists`) so the same model cannot grade its own work; set `allow_self_audit:true` to bypass. Default rubrics check factual grounding, constraint adherence, PII leak, internal consistency, open-question coverage, and actionability — override with `rubric`. With `cheap_mode:true` (default) the cheapest sufficient med-tier auditor is picked. Audit cost rolls up under `session_id` tagged `purpose:audit` so audit spend is distinct but unified.

output_to_audit.description: The text to audit. Either this or `session_id` is required.

session_id.description: If `output_to_audit` is omitted, the latest transcript for this session is loaded.

rubric.description: Override the default rubric. Pass an empty array or omit to use defaults.

producing_panelists.description: Provider names that produced the audited output; excluded from the auditor pool to avoid self-grading.

auditor.description: Explicit auditor provider. Overrides cheap-mode pick.

coalesce.description: Run audit through MULTIPLE judges in parallel and aggregate. Auto-enabled when `producing_panelists` covers every registered provider (otherwise the old 'no auditor' error path).

strict_mode.description: When true, item.pass requires ALL judges to pass that item (default is majority vote). Top-level `passed` then requires all items to pass.

max_judges.description: Cap on judges in coalesce mode (controls cost).

constraints.description: User constraints the output should respect; surfaced to the auditor.

stddev.description: Coalesce only: stddev of per-judge scores (N>=3) or null when N<3.

obvious_failure_judges.description: Coalesce only: judges who flagged this item below the obvious-failure threshold for its severity.

per_judge.description: Coalesce only: per-judge score/pass/rationale (or status when invalid).

obvious_failures.description: Coalesce only: rubric_item ids where any judge scored below the obvious-failure threshold (0.3 for high-severity, 0.2 for med).

disagreements.description: Coalesce only: rubric_item ids with stddev > 0.3 (N>=3) or range > 0.4 (N=2).

audit_process_failure.description: Coalesce only: true when fewer than ceil(N/2) judges returned valid output, so the audit itself failed (not the audited content).

create.description: End-to-end macro: ingest documents -> confer (scope) -> orchestrate (build) -> review -> audit, all under one session_id so usage/cost rolls up cleanly. Use this when you have a high-level instruction and want the full plan-build-review-audit lifecycle in one call. `documents` may be file paths or URLs (URLs go through the `fetch` allowlist). When audit fails (overall_score < audit_threshold), `create` injects the audit feedback as constraints and runs orchestrate ONE more time, then re-audits; `create_cheap` skips the retry. `target_path` writes the final deliverable to disk (unless `dry_run:true` or audit failed). Status is one of: success | audit_failed | audit_failed_after_retry | error.

instruction.description: High-level instruction; e.g. 'tie all features in the project to rules and regulations in the project documents'.

documents.description: File paths (relative to repo root) or URLs (resolved via `fetch`).

target_path.description: If set, the final deliverable is written here (parent dirs created).

dry_run.description: When true, never write to `target_path` (the deliverable is still in the response).

plan_only.description: Confer (scope) + orchestrate planner still run so you see the resolved DAG; workers / recombine / review / audit are ALL skipped. Returns the plan + cost estimate. Cheap way to preview a `create` run before committing to the spend.

create_cheap.description: Cheap-mode variant of `create`: cheap_mode defaults to true (sub-tasks route to the cheapest sufficient model per difficulty tier) AND the audit-failure retry is suppressed to honor cost. Otherwise identical contract to `create`.

update_crosscheck.description: Check whether a newer version of crosscheck-agent is available at https://github.com/fxspeiser/crosscheck-agent (compares local git HEAD against the remote main HEAD via the GitHub API). With apply=true, runs `git pull --ff-only` in the install directory; the MCP server cannot reload itself, so the response asks the user to restart Claude Code afterwards. Requires the install to be a git checkout with the standard remote. The first crosscheck tool call per server process automatically performs the same check (cached 6h) and attaches an `update_notice` to its result so Claude can surface the upgrade offer.

apply.description: When true, run `git pull --ff-only` in the install directory after confirming an update is available. The user must restart Claude Code (or the MCP connection) to load the new code.

recommend_panel.description: Smart-router: recommend the smallest effective provider panel for a given purpose, scored from usage_log history (reliability + cost + engagement). Cold-start (<5 calls of history) falls back to provider_stats win-rate. Use this directly, or pass `auto_panel: true` to confer/debate to delegate panel selection automatically.

purpose.description: Purpose to recommend a panel for; e.g. 'confer', 'debate', 'audit', 'worker'.

available_only.description: Restrict recommendations to providers currently registered with an API key in .env.

scoreboard.description: Read-only snapshot of accumulated provider performance and recent activity. Surfaces the per-repo win-rate that triangulate uses for weights, plus delegation counters and totals so a UI can render a 'who's winning here' panel.

top_k.description: Cap the number of providers in the leaderboard.

recent_limit.description: If > 0, include the last N event lines from events_log (post-redaction).

fetch.description: Retrieve a URL with allowlist enforcement and persist a sha256-keyed snapshot under .crosscheck/evidence/. Repeat fetches of the same URL return the cached snapshot unless force_refresh=true. Use this to ground claims with reproducible evidence.

bench.description: Run rule-based goldens against each provider in a panel and return a per-provider score + ranking. Bumps provider_stats wins/losses, which feeds the weights surfaced by triangulate. Use this to keep an honest, repo-scoped picture of who answers your repo's questions best.

providers.description: Panel to bench. Each golden is run once per provider in this list.

goldens_dir.description: Override the goldens directory (defaults to config.bench.goldens_dir).

filter.description: Run only goldens whose name contains this substring (case-insensitive).

review.description: Peer-review a code snippet or proposal across one or more LLMs.

session_id.description: Optional id to accumulate usage across calls.

untrusted_input.description: When true, treat the snippet as untrusted: wrap in tags, neutralize obvious injection phrases, instruct panelists to treat as data only. Use for snippets from outside contributors, user submissions, or anything you wouldn't run as a script.
